newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SingTel speeds up handphone investment.
newsitem.headline: SingTel speeds up handphone investment.

text.p: Singapore Telecommunications Ltd's (SingTel) told Reuters on Wednesday it was accelerating its investment spending on its digital handphone systems.
SingTel, which has lost its handphone and paging market monopoly on April 1, would spend more than Singapore $100 million this year instead of over the next two years as announced last August.

"Improving our digital mobile network coverage is our priority and we are committing more than S$100 million within this year to achieve this," Lung Chien Ping, chief executive officer of SingTel unit SingTel Mobile, said in a statement.
"We have reviewed the programme and will be accelerating it," a company spokeswoman told Reuters.
She said SingTel had spent S$860 million on all its cellular network systems to-date. About S$280 million of it was spent on its personal communications network system (PCN).
SingTel also said in the statement it would add at least 200 more PCN base stations to its current 400 over the next six months.
The company also said it would be cutting rates and enhancing packages for its PCN handphone users from May 1.
Just a week ago, SingTel Mobile announced price cuts for its global system for mobile communications (GSM) handphone users.

The new PCN package offered to new and existing customers includes more free air time, up to 12.5 percent lower monthly call charges, up to 20 percent lower incoming call charges and from June 1, free autoroam services to Malaysia.
"SingTel Mobile is also looking to extend this free (autoroam) service to other ASEAN countries so that PCN customers can use their handphones when they travel to these countries," Lung said.
ASEAN, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
